matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); you cannot rotate it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you relocate a stick, ensure the orientation remains the same.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick and turning it into a vertical stick, which creates an invalid character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When proposing a corrected equation, ensure the total number of sticks remains unchanged.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral and not placing it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each stick relocation, check that each character corresponds to a recognized symbol.
matchstick.example: Creating a string like "VIX", which is not a standard Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and check that the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After forming a candidate corrected equation, compute its numeric values to ensure it is true.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonal sticks and form a valid X or V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a diagonal stick from or to an X or V, ensure the resulting character still has two diagonals.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When outputting the answer, ensure the line follows the exact required format.
matchstick.example: Writing 'Correct version: XIV = XII + II' (missing the phrase "of the equation").

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change from the original can be achieved by moving exactly one stick (no more, no less).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, simulate the stick move to ensure only one stick is relocated.
matchstick.example: Changing "XIX = XII + II" to "XIV = XII + II" by altering two characters (X→V and adding a stick elsewhere), which would require more than one stick.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave an empty placeholder.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you take the sole vertical stick from an I, delete the I symbol.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from I and leaving a blank space, resulting in an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transformation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator (+, -, =), ensure the resulting operator is a valid symbol (e.g., turning '-' into '=' by adding a horizontal stick, or '-' into '+' by adding a vertical stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the solution involves changing an operator, consider moving a stick between operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' and ending up with an invalid operator combination.

matchstick.title: Intra‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different position within the same character, altering its shape (e.g., repositioning a diagonal stick in X to form V) while preserving orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a solution requires changing a numeral's shape without involving another character, consider moving a stick within that character.
matchstick.example: Assuming a stick must be transferred to another character, missing the possibility of reshaping X into V by moving one of its diagonals internally.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual changes and forgets to check whether the resulting Roman‑numeral equality is true.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a corrected equation, convert both sides to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality before finalizing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model generates a plausible answer but omits or alters the required final line syntax.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with exactly 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' using uppercase letters and collapsing whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character without placing it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure every removed stick is immediately placed on another character, preserving the total stick count.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick out of a numeral without guaranteeing the remaining strokes form a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick removal, verify that the source character still matches a legal numeral or operator; if not, the move is invalid.

matchstick.description: Proposed equation not reachable by a single stick move (multiple sticks changed)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model attempts to fix the equation by altering several characters, exceeding the one‑stick limit.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Simulate the exact stick relocation and confirm that only two characters (source and destination) are altered.
